[ASSISTANT_SAID] The GRE (Graduate Record Examinations) is a standardized test required for admission to many graduate schools in the United States.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The GRE consists of three main sections: Analytical Writing Assessment (AWA), Verbal Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Analytical Writing Assessment includes two tasks: Issue Task and Argument Task, each with a 30-minute time limit.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Verbal Reasoning section tests vocabulary, reading comprehension, and the ability to analyze and evaluate written material.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Quantitative Reasoning section tests basic math skills, including algebra, geometry, and data analysis.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The GRE is scored on a scale of 130-170 for Verbal and Quantitative sections, and 0-6 for Analytical Writing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The entire GRE test takes approximately 3 hours and 45 minutes to complete, including breaks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended preparation includes studying content, practicing with sample questions, and taking practice tests.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested online resources for GRE prep include Khan Academy, Magoosh GRE, Quantum GRE, ETS PowerPrep, GRE Guide, CrackAPL, and Varsity Tutors.
